name: Modern Horizons
credit: Archetypes and signpost uncommons as Wizards of the Coast showed them on Weekly MTG (listed on the MTG Wiki). Players' notes and key cards from Card Kingdom's archetype guide, Hipsters of the Coast, Limited Level-Ups and Star City Games, reworded.
about: Players rate it one of the deepest and hardest draft formats. The archetypes are loose, with a lot of cross-synergy, and many pairs have a second way to build. It is a format of one-, two- and four-mana creatures; boards stall, so mass pumps and removal matter. Changelings are strong early picks because they fit many decks. White was the weakest color. Snow is much better in draft than in sealed.

src.t: Modern Horizons draft tips (Hipsters of the Coast)
The Definitive Modern Horizons Draft Guide (Star City Games)

list.d: Creatures with enter-the-battlefield abilities, and ways to flicker them for more.
list.p: In practice it is less about forcing blink than playing good white-blue cards and picking up value from the occasional flicker.

list.d: Sneak Ninjas in with ninjutsu by returning an unblocked attacker.
list.p: Prioritize evasive creatures to carry ninjutsu. With no other creature around, just cast the Ninja.

list.d: Flood the board with Goblins and sacrifice them for value.
list.p: Goatnap plus Feaster of Fools is a strong pair.

list.d: Cycle and sacrifice lands, then get paid for the lands in your graveyard.
list.p: Keep count of enablers against payoffs, and use removal and tricks to reach the late game.

list.d: Rewards for creatures entering the battlefield; tokens count.
list.p: Boards often stall, so value the mass pumps highly.

list.d: Changelings, which count as every creature type, and cards that reward one chosen type.
list.p: Changelings work best supporting other decks, especially in sealed.

list.d: Cards that reward drawing your second card each turn, fed by cycling and card draw.
list.p: The real tempo deck: cycle something every turn to power up your attackers. You need few payoffs, since the draw effects alone out-card the opponent.

list.d: Fill your graveyard with creature cards, then exile or reanimate them for value.
list.p: Ransack the Lab and Winding Way get it going fast.

list.d: Slivers share their abilities with each other: go wide and buff the whole team.
list.p: A black splash adds Smiting Helix and Etchings of the Chosen.

list.d: Snow permanents, snow-covered lands included, power up snow payoffs.
list.p: One of the strongest draft decks. Take snow-covered lands early and often; it is much weaker in sealed.
